content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"The severity analysis can be traced from the findings to the conclusion, but the remedial-action conclusion ('immediate, appropriate, and effective action by investigating') does not follow from the documented evidence that S2 discontinued the investigations and deferred discipline, which the Agency's own Lulverne footnote flags without reconciling."},"rc2":{"status":"pass","note":"Material characterizations are tied to named witnesses (Complainant, S1, S2, S4, S5, C1, C2, C3) whose conflicting accounts are recorded, though the Agency's preponderance findings are not pinned to specific ROI pages (only one ROI citation appears) and S4's fact-finding output is described only through his own averment."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Most events are dated in sequence, from the October 2014 hire through the July 29, 2015 transfer and the EEO filing dates, but key remedial-timeline points are left unresolved: S5's visit (May vs. June 18–19, 2015), when S2 learned of the harassment ('April or May'), when the investigations were halted, and the date of the final decision."},"rc4":{"status":"review","note":"The decision rests on a stated severe-or-pervasive criterion and a prompt-remedial-action standard, but the individual decision-maker is not identified, the severity benchmark ('tend to include vulgar, sex-based epithets') is given without authority, and claim 6 and the evidence that S2 halted the investigation are not expressly weighed before finalization."},"rc5":{"status":"review","note":"The witness evidence is attributed in substantial detail, but the unexplained gap between the documented halted investigation and the remedial-action conclusion, together with the chronology ambiguities and the unidentified decision-maker, means an independent reviewer could not fully assess support for the decision without further context."}}}
